liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Opened with Jack Straw, played blazing fast and very hot, as everyone expected; Reviewer finds the first-set Jack Straw and China>Rider noteworthy [17][18]
- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Bird Song in the second set as awesome; Reviewer calls the Stranger, Bird Song and Playin' sequence exquisite, with psychedelic interplay between Jerry and Bob [14][18]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer finds the China>Rider particularly energetic in a first set with a cowboy theme [16]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Highlight is the jam out of Space into Not Fade Away, finding a groove well before vocals start [21]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer praises Wharf Rat, alongside Playin' and the Space into Not Fade Away, as outstanding [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-07-04.152650.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 157 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-07-04.140286.fob.nak300.vita.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 154 min [3]
- **gd81-07-04.sbd.samaritano-miller.21802.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 159 min; rated 4.22/5 by 18 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the matrix recording's sound quality superb and says it shows Brent and Jerry's interplay [14]
- **gd1981-07-04.175899.aud.benrstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 156 min [8]
- **gd81-07-04.nak700.clugston.2216.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 4.29/5 by 21 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers the soundboard to the audience tape, which is too bright, with drums and bass sometimes drowning everything [19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer drove from New York; it was high 90s, outdoors in late afternoon sun, with the Dead in Texas on the Fourth [17]
- Reviewer attended many Texas shows in the late seventies and early eighties and considers this the peak [22]
- Reviewer lived in Austin; fireworks during the set break sent smoke across the stage as the band returned [23]
- Band struggled to sing and rubbed their eyes, so the second set was cut short [23]
- Reviewer recalls a long line of cars, heat, fireworks, and barbecued turkey drumsticks sold around the infield [25]
- A drunk man in shorts and cowboy boots stood on a kitchen step near the stage yelling 'New Mexico!' and fell [25]
- Fireworks can be heard throughout the recording because it was the Fourth of July [1]
- Fireworks can be heard throughout the recording on the Fourth of July [3]
- Reviewer calls the show a relatively unknown gem, with a second set very different from the first [16]
- Second set has few songs and unusual song placement, yet the band plays very well [20]
- Reviewer says Brent put final touches on the band, making them better [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-07-04.152650.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII) [1]
- **gd1981-07-04.140286.fob.nak300.vita.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise and Scott Clugston; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM300 mics > Sony TC-D5 > Dat 16/48; Transfer Info: Dat 16/48 (Sony PCM-R500)… [3]. Also: Jim Vita made the master; Jim Wise did the transfer; a soundboard source patches 0:57 at the end of Drums [3]
- **gd81-07-04.sbd.samaritano-miller.21802.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano & Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard and Audience composite [5]. Also: Reviewer had an old cassette of the show from KUT, but finds this copy better [25]
- **gd1981-07-04.175899.aud.benrstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Master Cassettes Recorded by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer, Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited, Processed w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel December 20, 2025; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassettes (Maxell XLIIS-90's) [8]. Also: Taper Jon Bernstein recorded front-of-board and centered; gear is forgotten; Ray Ackerman transferred it, with a Jim Vita drums patch [8]
- **gd81-07-04.nak700.clugston.2216.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak CM700's [10]. Also: Reviewer first heard a scratchy, many-generations-removed cassette, then tracked down a better copy, which is this source; Reviewer's first Dead tape was a second-generation copy of the audience recording, given by a college friend [16][18]
